steps.what: Read the posted receipt for supplies received.
Count the inventory of supplies consumed at the store.
Judge whether that count matches the receipt.

tasks.design: The operator still counts the inventory of supplies received and consumed at the store, and still judges whether that count matches the receipt. A receipt line is already posted on the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with item, quantity received, lot, time and the poster's name, so the hunt for the delivery note is shorter. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The receipt sat on a paper delivery note at goods-in, so the operator hunted it before the count.
tasks.enabler_now: The operations record already holds a receipt line. Showing item, quantity received, lot, time and the poster's name is configuration of that record.
tasks.still_hard: The count of what was consumed is on the floor, beside the kettle. A missing line or a split delivery is still read by hand. The match is a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The operator sees the drum, the bag and what is left. A posted quantity cannot say what was actually consumed.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the store and the kettle. Less time goes to hunting a delivery note. The operator still counts supplies received and consumed, and still judges the match.

reach.task: Post the receipt line before the operator counts.
reach.learn: The line needs item, quantity received, lot, time and the poster's name, or the operator reads the paper note.

reach.task: Hear a count that does not match the receipt.
reach.learn: That talk stays in the room. The operator does not send the count.

reach.task: Sample a lot after the operator has counted it.
reach.learn: The store count is not a release. The inspector still samples.

evidence.claim: The operator counts supplies received and consumed at the store. A posted receipt can be read. The count and the match stay with the operator. Model knowledge. No named product in this digest inventories a chemical store.

Dutch works-council rules require consent for a system that monitors staff presence, behaviour or performance. This receipt lookup does not log how fast the operator counts or whether they were at the store.
A learning model inside a guard or a stop needs a conformity assessment under the machinery rules. This design has no model and does not touch the reactor stop.
No annex III point fits a receipt lookup. Article 6(1) high-risk status is for a safety component of machinery. This lookup is not that component.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is the operator's inventory of supplies received and consumed at the store beside the kettle. Goods-in posting, purchasing and batch release sit outside it. The stores clerk posts the receipt before this task starts.

Structured input: the stores clerk posts one receipt line on the {OPS_SYSTEM} with item, quantity received, lot, time and the poster's name. If the line is missing or free text, the operator reads the paper delivery note and that read is not shorter.

The count and the match stay with the operator. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. There is no commit, so there is no gate on a sent version. The prior that a small share is an outside act is refused: the operator does not send the count outside the organisation. A talk with the supervisor, if one happens, is inside the organisation.
Existing system runtime is not the operator's time. Upkeep is a small check that those five receipt fields are still posted.
unknowns: Whether this plant's receipt already has item, quantity received, lot, time and a poster's name, or only a paper delivery note.
Whether a mismatch is written on the operator's own sheet or said to the supervisor in the room.
research_questions: Does the stores clerk post the receipt before the operator counts, or only after?
What share of deliveries arrive with no line the operator can read?

already_counted.description: Reading a missing or free-text delivery note by hand, inside the remaining read.

incremental.description: Checking that the stores clerk still posts item, quantity received, lot, time and a name.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the receipt is often missing or free text, so the operator still hunts the delivery note and the read is not shorter. High: most lines carry item, quantity received, lot, time and a name, and only that hunt shrinks. The count at the store and the match stay. The high stays under the net after the field check.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still the store and the kettle. Less time goes to hunting a delivery note. The operator still counts the inventory and still judges the match.
reach: The stores clerk posts the receipt. The operator still counts what was consumed.
A supervisor may hear a mismatch in the room. That talk is not a send.
Nothing is sent outside the organisation, and no machine files the count.
skills_to_grow: Refuse a receipt line that does not name the item on the pallet.
Count the store when the posted quantity and the pallet disagree.
Keep the count as the operator's own record. Do not let a machine file it.
role.ambitious_version: The receipt line is already posted. The operator still counts the store and still judges the match, and no machine files the count.
